chapter.title: Class 10 History (India and the Contemporary World - II)
chapters_covered: Chapter 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
Chapter 3: The Making of a Global World
Chapter 5: Print Culture and the Modern World

terminology.meaning: A system of rule with no restraints on the power exercised; traditionally refers to a monarchical government that is centralized, militarized, and repressive.
A vision of a society that is so ideal that it is unlikely to actually exist.
A direct vote by which all the people of a region are asked to accept or reject a proposal.
The legal right to vote in political elections.
A political philosophy that stressed the importance of tradition, established institutions and customs, and preferred gradual development to quick change.
A customs union formed in 1834 at the initiative of Prussia and joined by most German states to abolish tariff barriers.
When an abstract idea (for instance, greed, envy, freedom, liberty) is expressed through a person or a thing.
A non-violent method of mass agitation based on the power of truth and the need to search for truth.
Labor that villagers were forced to contribute without any payment.
A form of demonstration or protest by which people block the entrance to a shop, factory, or office.
The refusal to deal and associate with people or participate in activities, or buy and use things; usually a form of protest.
A bonded laborer under contract to work for an employer for a specific amount of time to pay off passage to a new country/plantation.
Tax imposed on imported goods at the border of a country.
British laws restricting the import of foreign corn to protect domestic agricultural landlords.
The phase of large-scale international industrial production prior to and outside the factory system, organized in rural households.
A person who 'staples' or sorts wool according to its fiber.
A person who 'fulls'—that is, gathers—cloth by pleating.
The process in which fibers (such as cotton or wool) are prepared prior to spinning.
A paid agent appointed by the East India Company to supervise weavers, collect cloth, and examine quality.
A mechanical device used for weaving, operated by ropes and pulleys, which speeds up weaving and enables large-width cloth production.
The art of beautiful and stylized handwriting.
A parchment made from the skin of animals used for writing luxury manuscripts.
In letterpress printing, a flat wooden or metal board pressed onto the back of paper to get the impression from type.
A metal frame in which types were set and text composed in letterpress printing.
Beliefs which violate accepted religious teachings or dogma of the Church.
A formal Roman Catholic tribunal established for identifying, trying, and punishing heretics.
Cheap pocket-sized books sold by traveling peddlers known as chapmen in 16th-18th century Europe.
Low-priced small books printed in France on poor quality paper and bound in cheap blue covers.
A system of governance in which a single entity rules with absolute, unchecked power.
A legal pronouncement or ruling on Islamic law issued by a recognized religious authority (Ulema).

definitions.definition: A state in which the majority of its citizens, and not just its rulers, came to develop a sense of common identity and shared history or descent.
Political and economic doctrine emphasizing individual freedom, equality before the law, government by consent, and market deregulation.
Philosophy of non-violent resistance asserting that physical force is unnecessary when fighting for truth and justice.
Complete independence from colonial rule, formally resolved by the Indian National Congress at Lahore in December 1929.
A global financial mechanism wherein one country's trade deficit with a second nation is balanced by its trade surplus with a third nation.
Post-WWII monetary framework establishing fixed exchange rates pegged to the US Dollar, overseen by the IMF and World Bank.
Decentralized, merchant-funded manufacturing system operating in rural peasant homes prior to factory mechanization.
A veteran mill worker employed by factory owners to recruit new workers from rural villages and ensure their discipline.
The historical transformation in book production, reading habits, and public debate following Gutenberg's invention of movable type.
An official list compiled by the Roman Catholic Church starting in 1558 to censor books deemed heretical or dangerous.

concepts.title: Creation of French National Identity (1789)
concepts.description: Measures including la patrie, le citoyen, tricolour flag, National Assembly, centralized laws, standardized measures, and French language adoption.

concepts.title: Napoleonic Administrative System
concepts.description: Civil Code of 1804 granting legal equality, property security, feudal abolition, and guild removal across conquered European territories.

concepts.title: Romantic Nationalism
concepts.description: Cultural movement promoting emotion, intuition, folk songs, dances (polonaise/mazurka), and vernacular language over pure rationalism.

concepts.title: Balkan Explosive Geopolitics
concepts.description: Nationalist disintegration of Ottoman Balkan territories coupled with imperial rivalries (Russia, Germany, Austria-Hungary) triggering WWI.

concepts.title: Gandhian Satyagraha Triple Testing
concepts.description: Early localized non-violent struggles in Champaran (1917, indigo), Kheda (1917, revenue), and Ahmedabad (1918, mill workers).

concepts.title: Non-Cooperation to Civil Disobedience Progression
concepts.description: Transition from refusing cooperation with colonial institutions (1920-22) to actively breaking colonial statutes like the Salt Law (1930-34).

concepts.title: Biological Conquest of Americas
concepts.description: European conquest facilitated by deadly pathogens (smallpox) to which Native Americans lacked immunity, decimating communities.

concepts.title: Great Depression of 1929
concepts.description: Global economic collapse caused by post-WWI agricultural overproduction, Wall Street Crash, bank failures, and credit withdrawals.

concepts.title: Hand Labour vs Machine Preference
concepts.description: Victorian industrialists' preference for abundant, cheap human labor for seasonal work and customized products over expensive machinery.

concepts.title: Print as Engine of Enlightenment
concepts.description: Dissemination of scientific knowledge, political philosophies (Voltaire, Rousseau), and public debate leading to modern democratic movements.

facts.fact: Frédéric Sorrieu, a French artist, prepared a series of four prints in 1848 visualizing his dream of a world made up of 'democratic and social Republics'.
The Civil Code of 1804 is commonly known as the Napoleonic Code.
The Zollverein customs union formed in 1834 reduced the number of currencies in German states from over thirty to two.
Kaiser William I of Prussia was proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles on January 18, 1871.
The influenza epidemic and crop failures of 1920-1921 killed 12 to 13 million people in India.
General Dyer ordered the Jallianwala Bagh firing in Amritsar on April 13, 1919 (Baisakhi Day).
Mahatma Gandhi's Salt March covered 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi over 24 days with 78 volunteers.
Irish Potato Famine (1845-1849) caused around 1,000,000 people to die of starvation when disease destroyed the potato crop.
Rinderpest (cattle plague) arrived in Africa in the late 1880s and killed 90 percent of native African cattle.
Henry Ford introduced assembly line mass production at his Detroit car plant, pricing Model T as the first affordable car.
James Hargreaves invented the Spinning Jenny in 1764.
Seth Hukumchand set up the first Indian jute mill in Calcutta in 1917.
Buddhist Diamond Sutra (AD 868) is the oldest printed book in Japan.
Johann Gutenberg printed approximately 180 copies of the Bible on his first movable type press around 1448.
James Augustus Hickey began publishing the Bengal Gazette in 1780 as a weekly political paper independent of company influence.
Rashsundari Debi wrote 'Amar Jiban' (1876), the first full-length autobiography published in the Bengali language.

people.name: Frédéric Sorrieu
people.role: French artist who painted 1848 utopian prints of worldwide democratic republics.

people.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
people.role: French military leader and Emperor who introduced administrative reforms across Europe.

people.name: Duke Metternich
people.role: Austrian Chancellor who hosted the Congress of Vienna in 1815 and spearheaded European conservatism.

people.name: Giuseppe Mazzini
people.role: Italian revolutionary founder of Young Italy and Young Europe advocating unified republican Italy.

people.name: Otto von Bismarck
people.role: Prussian Chief Minister who executed the 'Blood and Iron' strategy to unify Germany.

people.name: Count Cavour
people.role: Prime Minister of Sardinia-Piedmont who engineered diplomatic unification of Italy.

people.name: Giuseppe Garibaldi
people.role: Italian nationalist military leader who led the 'Red Shirts' in the Expedition of the Thousand (1860).

people.name: Mahatma Gandhi
people.role: Leader of Indian national movement who introduced Satyagraha, Non-Cooperation, and Civil Disobedience.

people.name: Baba Ramchandra
people.role: Sanyasi and former indentured worker in Fiji who led Awadh peasant revolt against landlords.

people.name: Alluri Sitarama Raju
people.role: Tribal leader in Andhra Pradesh Gudem Hills who led guerrilla struggle against forest laws.

people.name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
people.role: Leader of Depressed Classes Association who fought for political rights and signed Poona Pact (1932).

people.name: Abanindranath Tagore
people.role: Indian painter who created famous 1905 iconographic portrait of Bharat Mata.

people.name: Henry Ford
people.role: American industrialist pioneer of assembly line mass production at Detroit car factory.

people.name: Richard Arkwright
people.role: English inventor who created the centralized cotton mill bringing machinery under one roof.

people.name: Dwarkanath Tagore
people.role: 19th-century Bengal merchant who set up six joint-stock companies in the 1830s-40s.

people.name: Jamsetjee Nusserwanjee Tata
people.role: Pioneer Indian industrialist who founded massive textile mills and TISCO (1907).

people.name: Johann Gutenberg
people.role: German inventor from Mainz who developed movable type mechanical printing press in 1448.

people.name: Martin Luther
people.role: German religious reformer who wrote 95 Theses (1517) initiating Protestant Reformation.

people.name: Rammohun Roy
people.role: Indian social reformer who published Sambad Kaumudi (1821) against Sati and caste abuses.

people.name: Jyotiba Phule
people.role: Maharashtra social reformer who wrote Gulamgiri (1873) exposing caste oppression.

places.significance: Palace Hall of Mirrors where Kaiser William I was proclaimed German Emperor on Jan 18, 1871.
Site of St. Paul's Church where 831 elected representatives convened German National Assembly in 1848.
District in Bihar where Gandhi launched his first Indian satyagraha for indigo farmers in 1917.
Enclosed ground in Amritsar where British troops under General Dyer opened fire on peaceful crowd on April 13, 1919.
Coastal village in Gujarat where Gandhi broke colonial salt law on April 6, 1930.
Town in Gorakhpur, UP, where violent burning of police station led to withdrawal of Non-Cooperation (1922).
New Hampshire location of 1944 UN Financial Conference establishing IMF and World Bank.
Pre-colonial western Indian port connecting trade routes to Gulf and Red Sea ports.
German city where Johann Gutenberg perfected the movable metal type printing press.
Location where Portuguese Jesuit priests introduced the first printing press to India in 1557.

dates_events.event: French Revolution begins, introducing popular sovereignty and national identity.
Napoleonic Code (Civil Code) enacted across French-controlled Europe.
Defeat of Napoleon at Waterloo; Congress of Vienna hosted by Metternich.
Treaty of Constantinople recognizes Greece as an independent nation.
Zollverein (Customs Union) established under Prussian leadership.
Revolutions across Europe; Frankfurt Parliament convenes in St. Paul Church.
Victor Emmanuel II proclaimed King of United Italy.
Proclamation of German Empire with Kaiser William I at Versailles.
Mahatma Gandhi returns to India from South Africa.
Jallianwala Bagh Massacre in Amritsar under General Dyer.
Nagpur Congress session adopts Non-Cooperation Programme.
Chauri Chaura incident occurs; Gandhi suspends Non-Cooperation Movement.
Simon Commission arrives in India and faces nationwide 'Go Back Simon' protests.
Lahore Congress session under Jawaharlal Nehru passes Purna Swaraj resolution.
Gandhi reaches Dandi and breaks Salt Law, launching Civil Disobedience Movement.
Poona Pact signed between Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Berlin Conference held where European powers carved up Africa.
Wall Street Crash in US marks onset of Great Depression.
Bretton Woods Conference establishes IMF and World Bank.
James Hargreaves invents the Spinning Jenny in England.
Seth Hukumchand sets up first Indian jute mill in Calcutta.
Diamond Sutra printed in Japan (oldest dated printed book).
Gutenberg perfects movable metal type printing press in Mainz.
Martin Luther writes Ninety-Five Theses criticizing Catholic Church practices.
James Augustus Hickey starts publishing Bengal Gazette.
Vernacular Press Act passed by Lord Lytton in India.

institutions.name: National Assembly (France)
institutions.purpose: Elected legislative body of citizens created during French Revolution.

institutions.name: Zollverein
institutions.purpose: Prussian-led customs union uniting German states economically.

institutions.name: Frankfurt Parliament
institutions.purpose: National Assembly of 831 elected German representatives meeting at St. Paul Church in 1848.

institutions.name: Oudh Kisan Sabha
institutions.purpose: Peasant association formed in Oct 1920 by Jawaharlal Nehru and Baba Ramchandra.

institutions.name: Swaraj Party
institutions.purpose: Political party formed within Congress in 1922 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru to contest council elections.

institutions.name: FICCI (Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry)
institutions.purpose: National body of Indian commercial and industrial interests established in 1927.

institutions.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
institutions.purpose: Bretton Woods institution created in 1944 to deal with external financial surpluses and deficits of member nations.

institutions.name: World Bank (IBRD)
institutions.purpose: Bretton Woods institution created in 1944 to finance post-war economic reconstruction.

institutions.name: Group of 77 (G-77)
institutions.purpose: Coalition of developing nations formed to demand a New International Economic Order (NIEO).

institutions.name: Deoband Seminary
institutions.purpose: Islamic seminary founded in 1867 publishing lithographic fatwas for Muslim code of conduct.

laws_systems.details: Abolished privileges based on birth, established equality before law, and secured property rights.
Colonial legislation allowing detention of political prisoners for up to two years without judicial trial.
Colonial statute restricting Assam tea garden plantation workers from leaving without permission.
British tariffs restricting foreign grain imports, repealed in 1846 following urban protests.
Global trade mechanism balancing trade deficits against trade surpluses across multiple nations.
Post-war financial framework based on fixed exchange rates pegged to the gold-convertible US dollar ($35/ounce).
East India Company practice providing loans to Indian weavers in exchange for exclusive cloth supply.
Roman Catholic Church censorship list prohibiting reading of heretical texts.
Colonial censorship law modeled on Irish Press Laws giving government power to seize seditious vernacular presses.

chronology.event: Battle of Waterloo & Congress of Vienna.
Greek War of Independence ending in Treaty of Constantinople.
Formation of the Zollverein Customs Union.
Unification of Italy under Cavour and Garibaldi.
Unification of Germany led by Bismarck.
Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.
Wall Street Crash & Great Depression launch.
Lahore Congress adopts Purna Swaraj Resolution.
Bretton Woods Conference establishes IMF & World Bank.
Formation of G-77 and demand for NIEO.

cause_effect.effect: Cheap foreign grain flooded Britain, causing land abandonment, rural unemployment, and massive emigration to Americas/Australia.
Perishable meat transported cheaply over long sea voyages, lowering European meat prices and diversifying working-class diet.
Wiped out 90% of native cattle, destroying pastoral livelihoods and forcing Africans into colonial wage labor.
Severed US raw cotton shipments to Britain, causing British buyers to buy Indian cotton at exorbitant prices, depriving local weavers.
Diverted British factory output to war supplies, causing British cloth imports to India to drop and stimulating Indian mill production.

cause_effect.cause: Invention of Movable Type Printing Press by Gutenberg (1448)
cause_effect.effect: Drastically reduced book production cost and time, creating a reading public and catalyzing the Protestant Reformation.
Challenged Roman Catholic Church abuses, leading to Protestant Reformation and new religious translation of scriptures.
Violent mob burned police station killing 22 policemen, prompting Gandhi to suspend Non-Cooperation Movement.

items: Flow of Capital (short and long-term investments)
Germania (Germany - heroism, oak crown, sword, eagle breastplate)

geographical_features.significance: Multi-ethnic mountainous region in Southeastern Europe (modern Romania, Bulgaria, Albania, Greece, Macedonia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Slovenia, Serbia, Montenegro) under Ottoman decline.
Site of tribal guerrilla insurgency led by Alluri Sitarama Raju against British forest restrictions.
Pre-colonial Indian port towns connecting maritime trade with Gulf, Red Sea, and Southeast Asian ports.
Route of Mahatma Gandhi's 1930 Salt March.

historical_concepts.explanation: The historical process where fragmented dynastic fiefdoms unified into territorial sovereign nation-states backed by centralized administrative institutions.
Grassroots movements led by peasants, tribals, and plantation workers who interpreted Swaraj through their own local anti-oppression frameworks.
The deployment of infectious diseases (smallpox, rinderpest) as unintentional or intentional biological tools of conquest against vulnerable isolated populations.
Decentralized international trade networks linking urban capital with rural household craft production before the establishment of factory systems.
The creation of an open social space where citizens discuss politics, challenge authority, and cultivate public opinion through mass printed media.

civic_concepts.explanation: The political principle that legitimate state authority is created and sustained by the consent of its citizens, who form the ultimate source of power.
Active, non-violent refusal to comply with unjust colonial laws or demands as a political tactic to force reform.
The fundamental democratic right of journalists and citizens to publish news, opinions, and critiques without state censorship.
The constitutional guarantee that every individual is subject to the same legal code without special privileges based on birth or class.

economic_concepts.explanation: An economic alliance eliminating internal tariffs among member states to create a unified domestic market and facilitate trade.
An international payment mechanism allowing a nation to offset trade deficits with one trading partner using surpluses earned from another.
Industrial manufacturing system pioneered by Henry Ford where products move continuously past stationary workers, drastically lowering unit costs.
Severe worldwide economic downturn characterized by collapsing asset prices, bank failures, mass unemployment, and trade contraction.
Proposals advanced by the G-77 developing countries to revise global trade rules, securing fair raw material prices and resource sovereignty.
